outcome: Vaginal delivery vs. cesarean delivery after labor induction in women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy
cohort: 1,357 women with singleton pregnancies, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, and who underwent induction of labor at 34 weeks of gestation or more from January 1, 2002, to March 31, 2013
finding: A prediction model using eight variables (maternal age, BMI, gestational age, intrapartum magnesium sulfate use, need for cervical ripening, prior cesarean delivery and cervical dilation, and effacement) showed satisfactory discrimination in predicting cesarean delivery risk in women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy undergoing labor induction.
mod_finding: The study aimed to identify characteristics associated with vaginal delivery compared with cesarean delivery after labor induction in women with hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
